macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Stocks fall as oil prices surge and Treasury yields hit multi-decade highs
items.summary: U.S. stocks came under pressure as Brent crude rose above $105 a barrel amid Middle East tensions and long-term Treasury yields reached levels not seen in more than two decades. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all declined in the latest session.[1][3][6]

items.title: Fed minutes signal another rate hike could come before year-end
items.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September meeting showed that most officials believed another interest-rate increase would probably be needed this year because inflation remained elevated and progress toward the 2% target had stalled.[4][5]

items.title: Long-term Treasury yields reach 24-year highs
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield reportedly reached 5.364%, while the 30-year yield rose to about 5.70%, increasing borrowing costs and weighing particularly on technology and financial shares.[5][9]

items.title: Paramount completes $81 billion Warner Bros. takeover
items.summary: Paramount, under its Skydance ownership, completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating a major new Hollywood media company.[4]

items.title: PepsiCo beats quarterly expectations but lowers full-year outlook
items.summary: PepsiCo reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and profit, but its shares and investors focused on the company’s reduced full-year earnings outlook.[8]

items.title: Chipotle rises on report Starbucks explored an acquisition
items.summary: Chipotle shares gained more than 6% after a report said Starbucks had explored acquiring the fast-casual restaurant chain, citing people familiar with the matter.[8]

items.title: Wolfspeed gains after proposed $1.5 billion government loan commitment
items.summary: Wolfspeed shares jumped after the U.S. Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital announced a conditional $1.5 billion loan commitment for the semiconductor company.[9]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $83,000 amid risk-off trading
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $83,000 as higher Treasury yields, rising oil prices and geopolitical tensions pressured risk assets. Ether, XRP and Dogecoin also declined, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $484.9 million in net outflows, their largest one-day withdrawal since June 25.

items.title: U.S. government transfers $770 million in Bitcoin to Coinbase Prime
items.summary: The U.S. government transferred 9,261 BTC, worth approximately $770 million, to Coinbase Prime over two days, according to Galaxy Research. The movement coincided with weakness in Bitcoin’s price, though the transfer’s intended purpose was not specified.

items.title: EU regulators set deadline for noncompliant stablecoin services
items.summary: The European Securities and Markets Authority told crypto firms to stop offering services linked to stablecoins that do not comply with the EU’s MiCA framework. National regulators must ensure remaining exposures are addressed by January 8, 2027.

items.title: Abstract announces phased shutdown of Ethereum Layer 2
items.summary: Ethereum Layer 2 network Abstract announced that it will gradually cease operations after nearly three years, with formal closure scheduled for December 15, 2026. Users were instructed to migrate their assets before the shutdown.

items.title: Coinbase completes Deribit integration and plans Coinbase Pro relaunch
items.summary: Coinbase completed the integration of crypto options exchange Deribit and plans to relaunch Coinbase Pro before the end of 2026. The move expands Coinbase’s derivatives and professional trading infrastructure.

items.title: Ethereum rallies 18% in 24 hours
items.summary: Ether surged roughly 18% over 24 hours to above $2,250 during Asian trading, leading a broad cryptocurrency market rally. Separate market data showed ETH later trading below $2,700 with gains narrowing, indicating elevated volatility.

items.title: South Korea proposes broader tokenized-securities framework
items.summary: South Korea’s Financial Services Commission announced proposed revisions that would expand the range of securities eligible for tokenization, including stocks, bonds and funds.

items.title: Hashi Bitcoin finance network announces October rollout
items.summary: Hashi, a Bitcoin finance network built by Mysten Labs, is set to begin a phased rollout in October with more than $500 million in capital commitments from launch partners, according to the Sui Foundation.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Odyssey launches Odyssey-3 world model
items.summary: Boston-based AI company Odyssey launched Odyssey-3, a world-model research preview, adding to the latest wave of generative models for simulated environments.[1]

items.title: ASI wins $99 million U.S. Army AI contract
items.summary: ASI announced a five-year, $99 million Army Enterprise IDIQ contract to scale its AI forecasting software across command-and-control operations.[1]

items.title: Mistral unveils Large 4 multimodal model
items.summary: Mistral AI introduced Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts multimodal model, with public preview access and open weights planned later in October.[2]

items.title: Reflection AI announces Beam open-weight model
items.summary: Reflection AI announced Beam, a 501-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model designed for coding, reasoning and agentic work; Apache 2.0 weights are expected later this month.[2]

items.title: Google releases EmbeddingGemma 2
items.summary: Google released EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740-million-parameter open embedding model that represents text, code, images, audio and video in a shared vector space and is designed to run on phones.[2]

items.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 and Intelligent UI
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly launched GPT-6 alongside Intelligent UI features that let ChatGPT generate interactive charts, calculators, buttons and mini-applications within responses.[2][3]

items.title: Google opens SynthID Detector
items.summary: Google made SynthID Detector available for public use, allowing uploads of images, video and audio to check for compatible AI-generated-media watermarks.[4]

items.title: Coalition commits $1.8 billion to virtual-cell AI
items.summary: A coalition involving Biohub, Google DeepMind, Meta and Isomorphic Labs committed roughly $1.8 billion toward building a predictive AI model capable of simulating cellular behavior and treatment responses.[6]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day launches on Xbox and PC
items.summary: Microsoft released Gears of War: E-Day for Xbox Series X|S and PC on October 6, with availability through Xbox Game Pass Ultimate.

items.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer released
items.summary: Fuse Games launched Star Wars: Galactic Racer on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. The game is also reportedly available at no additional cost to eligible Amazon subscribers.

items.title: Forza Horizon 6 PS5 version delayed to 2027
items.summary: The PlayStation 5 release of Forza Horizon 6 has been delayed to 2027 and is expected to launch alongside the game's first premium expansion.

items.title: Remedy begins full-scale development on Max Payne 1&2 Remake
items.summary: Remedy Entertainment has moved the Max Payne 1&2 Remake into full-scale development in collaboration with Rockstar Games. Swedish actor Alec Toselli was reportedly identified in the cast.

items.title: Microsoft appoints former Reddit executive to lead Minecraft
items.summary: Maria Angelidou-Smith, formerly Reddit's chief product officer, is joining Microsoft in a leadership role overseeing Minecraft.

items.title: Riot announces Game Changers Americas LCQ format
items.summary: Riot Games published the format and schedule for the 2026 Game Changers Americas Last Chance Qualifier, which will determine the region's second qualifier for the São Paulo championship.

items.title: Google and Unity expand AI game-development tools
items.summary: Google's experimental Playground platform enables simple games to be created through generative AI, while Unity announced a related partnership called Unity Spark for text-based game-content creation.

items.title: Xbox reportedly secures GTA VI cloud-streaming rights
items.summary: Reports say Xbox Cloud Gaming will offer Grand Theft Auto VI on supported consoles, televisions, and mobile devices, although the game is not planned for PC at launch.

items.title: Activision Blizzard esports faces layoffs amid Overwatch League uncertainty
items.summary: Activision Blizzard's esports division has reportedly suffered layoffs while team owners prepare to vote on the future format of the Overwatch League.

items.title: Mafia III receives free current-generation performance update
items.summary: Mafia III received a surprise update enabling 60 frames per second on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S; existing owners receive the upgrade at no extra cost.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Amazon completes 1,000th Project Kuiper satellite
items.summary: Amazon says it has built its 1,000th low-Earth-orbit satellite and expects its satellite internet service to begin within weeks. The milestone advances the company’s effort to compete with established broadband satellite networks.

items.title: Apple confirms October 13 launch event
items.summary: Apple confirmed a “Welcome home” event in New York on October 13, signaling an upcoming hardware or product announcement. The company has not disclosed the specific products that will be unveiled.

items.title: U.S. states sue TP-Link over router security disclosures
items.summary: Attorneys general from Florida, Iowa, Montana and Nebraska sued TP-Link, alleging deceptive marketing of router security and inadequate disclosure of ties to China. The case adds to growing scrutiny of networking equipment security and supply-chain relationships.

items.title: Samsung reports sharp preliminary profit increase
items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported preliminary third-quarter operating profit of about $80.1 billion, up roughly 782% year over year, while revenue rose about 127%. Both figures reportedly fell slightly short of analyst expectations.

items.title: Ring unveils Smart Lock and five cameras
items.summary: Amazon’s Ring introduced a $249 Smart Lock featuring a physical dial that recharges its battery when turned, alongside five new cameras. The smart lock is scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2027.
